props.title: One Pixel, All at Once

B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab sprite scene (teal test sprite, scale to fit), shader lab-shaders/02-hook-wobble.gdshader assigned at t=2.0 s (--material-at 2.0), 10 s, 30 fps, Forward+, no input.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'One Pixel, All at Once' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: the teal test sprite sits flat and still for two seconds, then a shader is switched on and it wobbles. Label: 'same scene, shader switched on'.
B01.motion_claim: The sprite is still, then comes alive the moment the shader switches on.

show.event: shader switches on; the sprite starts to wobble

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a flat versus lively sprite
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of 'looks flat' versus 'looks alive'; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: Two boxes on the cream stage. Left, 'your game code · CPU' with a small teal sprite icon and the words 'what exists, where'. Right, 'the shader · GPU' with the same icon, now with a wobble drawn around it, and 'how each part looks'. One arrow, left to right.
B02.motion_claim: The sprite icon is placed on the left, travels along the arrow and arrives restyled on the right.

show.event: restyled icon in the right box

B02.why: A two-box handoff is the whole claim; an icon that visibly changes on arrival says it with motion.

B03.visual_intent: A 12-by-6 grid of outline cells. Top: one dot-worker colours the cells one after another, a counter ticking. Bottom: a crowd of dots colours all 72 cells in the same instant. Labels: 'CPU: one job after another', 'GPU: the same job at once'.
B03.motion_claim: One worker sweeps the grid cell by cell while the whole second grid fills at once.

show.event: crowd fills the second grid at once

B03.why: A grid filled one cell at a time versus all at once is the CPU/GPU difference, as motion.

props.title: The slow way: a GDScript loop
props.note: 2,073,600 calls for one 1920 by 1080 picture · Godot 4.7.2

B04.visual_intent: The real loop from evidence/planning-checks/verify.gd on a cream code card, with the call count underneath.
B04.motion_claim: Line focus steps down the loop as it is described; the count lands last.
B04.why: LectureCodeTrace's paced line focus matches the sentence; the shell has no per-line cue.

B05.visual_intent: A horizontal time axis from 0 to 60 ms. A vertical budget line at 16.7 ms labelled 'one frame at 60 per second'. A bar grows along the axis, passes the line and stops at about 55, labelled 'the loop · about 55 ms'. Small grey credit: 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · five runs: 52 to 58 ms'.
B05.motion_claim: The bar grows past the budget line and keeps going.
B05.why: A bar crossing a line shows 'over budget'; a table only lists the numbers.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · the shader on the left

B06.capture_spec: C02: Lab rect, lab-shaders/01-gradient.gdshader, still PNG 1920x1080 (probes: 0.0196 / 0.498 / 0.9804 at x = 0.02 / 0.5 / 0.98).
B06.visual_intent: Code card with the four-line shader at left; at right a real Godot window showing a black-to-red gradient with a thin 0 to 1 ramp under it.
B06.motion_claim: The line is highlighted, then the red ramp is traced left to right under the gradient.

show.event: COLOR line highlighted; ramp marker sweeps

B06.why: Code and its result side by side is the claim: one line, the whole picture.

B07.visual_intent: 'game code · CPU' box at left, 'shader · GPU' box at right. An arrow between them labelled 'hands over the job · about 0.04 ms'. Under the GPU box, in grey: 'its own time: not readable on this setup'. Small credit: 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2'.
B07.motion_claim: A tiny package travels the arrow; the GPU box fills with pixels while the CPU box stays nearly empty.
B07.why: A handoff arrow with a speck of a cost label shows the idea; the grey note keeps the claim honest.

B08.visual_intent: A 16-by-9 pixel grid of outline cells. One cell gets a terracotta ring and a small code card beside it ('COLOR = …'). Then every cell takes its ramp color at once, left to right, the card staying put. Label: 'one pixel's rule → every pixel'.
B08.motion_claim: One ringed pixel, then the whole grid changes in the same instant.

show.event: grid, one cell ringed, code card
all cells take their color at once

B08.why: This is the film's central claim; only a grid shows 'one rule, every pixel' at a glance.
